messages.subject: lavaan vs lm: standard errors
parts:
Hey everyone,

I was using lavaan to constrain some of the regression weights in a multiple regression analysis. For this regression, I used the lm function in R and got this output:

Call:
lm(formula = y ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x1_x2 + x1_x3 + x2_x3 + x1_x2_x3, 
    data = test)

Residuals:
     Min       1Q   Median       3Q      Max 
-1.46310 -0.44001 -0.05495  0.42998  1.82083 

Coefficients:
              Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
(Intercept)  3.0813718  0.0810411  38.022  < 2e-16 ***
x1          -0.4747433  0.1119228  -4.242 3.98e-05 ***
x2           0.0009401  0.0392395   0.024    0.981    
x3           0.0158061  0.0345529   0.457    0.648    
x1_x2        0.1163471  0.0564131   2.062    0.041 *  
x1_x3       -0.0848979  0.0514304  -1.651    0.101    
x2_x3       -0.0037745  0.0117201  -0.322    0.748    
x1_x2_x3     0.0113530  0.0245033   0.463    0.644


Then I fit the same model with lavaan; the point esimtates were the same, but the standard errors were smaller in the lavaan output (e.g., .109 vs. .112 for x_1):


Parameter Estimates:

  Information                                 Expected
  Standard Errors                             Standard

Regressions:
                   Estimate  Std.Err  Z-value  P(>|z|)   Std.lv  Std.all
  y ~                                                                   
    x1               -0.475    0.109   -4.360    0.000   -0.475   -0.335
    x2                0.001    0.038    0.025    0.980    0.001    0.003
    x3                0.016    0.034    0.470    0.638    0.016    0.051
    x1_x2             0.116    0.055    2.120    0.034    0.116    0.221
    x1_x3            -0.085    0.050   -1.697    0.090   -0.085   -0.176
    x2_x3            -0.004    0.011   -0.331    0.741   -0.004   -0.029
    x1_x2_x3          0.011    0.024    0.476    0.634    0.011    0.042

Intercepts:
                   Estimate  Std.Err  Z-value  P(>|z|)   Std.lv  Std.all
    y                 3.081    0.079   39.079    0.000    3.081    4.348

Variances:
                   Estimate  Std.Err  Z-value  P(>|z|)   Std.lv  Std.all
    y                 0.417    0.048    8.660    0.000    0.417    0.831



I tried tweaking the lavaan settings (likelihood = "wishart", information = "observed", ...) but I never got the same standard errors as in the lm output. Is there any way to chose the settings in lavaan to obtain the same standard errors as in lm?
This is possibly more a general SEM question than a specific lavaan question, but I hope you can still help me out.

Best,
Andreas

messages.author: b8fd92e5e3662745
messages.subject: Re: lavaan vs lm: standard errors
parts:
lm computes the standard errors using s^2 (X'X)^{-1} / (n-p) unbiased formula. lavaan has to rely on the general ML expressions, which boil down to s^2 (X'X)^{-1} / n.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: lavaan vs lm: standard errors
parts:
See this set of slides:

http://users.ugent.be/~yrosseel/lavaan/zurich2015/lavaan_zurich2015.pdf

in particular slide 42.

From the lm fit, you can compute $\sigma^2$ as follows:

sum(resid(fit)^2) / nobs(fit)
# 2075.1

and you get the ML estimate reported by lavaan. If you didive by 'n - (p
+ 1)', you get

sum(resid(fit)^2) / (nobs(fit) - 5)
# 2184.316

and the sqrt of this number (46.73666) is wat lm's summary reports as
the residual standard error.

That is all there is to it: a different 'estimate' of $\sigma$, which is
used to scale the standard errors.

Yves.
